newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor stock price gains solidly based.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor stock price gains solidly based.

text.p: The strong advance of Portuguese cement firm Cimpor is solidly based on the good prospects for the sector and there should be more upside for its shares even if analysts are divided on just how much.

Analysts attributed recent gains, some 10 percent over the past month, to strong foreign interest attracted by the sector's capacity to generate cashflow, the 125 escudo divided and the possibility the country could soon be promoted to the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Europe index.

The stock was up 0.19 percent at 3,705 escudos on Wednesday, moving against the an overall weaker bourse trend, and most analysts contacted by Reuters expected it comfortably to exceed 4,000 escudos within the next 12 months.
"The international funds have money to invest and are reinforcing their positions in the more liquid stocks," said James Harrison of Lisbon brokers Midas Corretora.
Portugal Telecom, Banco Comercial Portugues and Sonae Investimentos, amongst others, are some (other) stocks being chosen by foreigners," he added.
After surging at the start of the year -- the stock hit a record 3,930 escudos in January -- Cimpor underperformed the market when investors reacted badly to its 1996 results.
Overall the stock has still only gained 11.5 percent this year against a 23 percent rise for the PSI20 index of leading stocks.
"The company was pretty penalised by its 'net profit', but investors forgot that the cashflow was more important," said one international analyst who asked not to be named.
Harrison said that he had a price target of 4,500 escudos for Cimpor by the end of the year.
"During three months, Cimpor was lagging well behind the index...the good chances of Portugal's entry into the MSCI have contributed to its recovery," the analyst said.
There has been speculation that Portugal could be switched to the Europe index from the emerging market group after the privatisation of state electricity concern EDP set for June.
Jose Freire, of Espirito Santo Research (ESR), said that he considered the company a good medium term investment and that research group was maintaining its buy recommendation.
But he noted that the company was not trading at a discount to other European cement companies.
"The price will only go above 3,800 escudos in 1997 if cement consumption showed really extraordinary growth, something which could happen," he said.

Cement consumption rose 22.4 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997. Economic growth is likely to be slightly quicker than initially expected in Portugal, with this year's local elections another reason for optimism that cement consumption will be strong, analysts say.

"The prospects for the cement sector in 1997 and 1998 are good and its international purchases are going to start to yield fruit," said analyst Pedro Assuncao, of Central de Investimentos, referring to recent foreign investment by the firm.
